title: Dynamic plug-in infrastructure
body:
DroneCore has its functionality built with compile-time plug-ins such as `Action`, `Mission`, `Telemetry`, etc. When DroneCore is built, we can choose which plug-ins we're interested in. Build chooses plug-ins in `plugins` directory and generates `DevicePluginContainer` class and methods to access to the "choosen" plug-in objects. It is necessary to build DroneCore if we wanted to add a new plug-in to it.

We're interested to add new plug-ins which DroneCore will pick it up run-time. Theoretical approach for this is [here](https://px4.slack.com/archives/C68J8H32A/p1506435370000733).

However, as we're interested to developing language bindings using gRPC; gRPC requires `.proto` files for each of the plug-in to be known at compile-time.
We're yet to investigate the feasibility of both (gRPC & dynamic plug-in). 

Updates on this activity will posted here.

title: TCP connection drop causes high CPU usage
body:
I connected DroneCore to a TCP server using `add_tcp_connection()`. If the added TCP connection drops, DroneCore will just spin in `receive()` of `TcpConnection`, because `recv()` returns immediately with 0. This causes 100% CPU load and shouldn't be desired behavior when the socket is disconnected.

I've fixed the issue by just setting `_should_exit` flag when `recv()` returns with 0 in receive thread. Certainly not the best solution but does the job for me. The dead connection still stays in DroneCore's connection list, so it would be nice if it could either be reopened manually through API or DroneCore tries to keep up connections itself.

title: Different connections to the same system
body:
I have a MAVLink-enabled autopilot that I'm connecting to from a PC using MAVSDK. I'd like to communicate with the AP using two different connections, one USB and one UART. I can connect to the AP using either one, but it doesn't seem that I'm able to connect to both at the same time.

Specifically, my approach is to call `add_any_connection` twice and get two different `System` pointers. From those pointers, I want to create two `MavlinkPassthrough`s so that I can send custom MAVLink messages directly to the device.

Is this possible? If it is, what kind of approach should I take?

Thank you!

comments.body:
Hmm, that's not how the MAVSDK architecture works. A system is a representation for a MAVLink system. You only have one system, and two connections to it.

Why do you want to have two MavlinkPassthrough instances? Do you want outgoing messages to be sent on both connections (which it ought to do unless something is broken), or do you want to send specific messages on either one or the other connection?
Hi @julianoes , thanks for replying. If it's possible, I'd like to send some messages over one connection, and some over a different connection exclusively.
Are you trying to achieve some kind of multihoming? Like having redundancy between two different links (e.g. both a radio link and an Internet link), such that messages go through the "best" path?

@JonasVautherin @julianoes I appreciate the questions, but unfortunately that's as much detail as I can give right now :(

I'll admit that I'm not extremely familiar with the architecture of MAVSDK, but how hard would it be for a system to maintain and choose between two connections?

What does a `System` require of a connection after initialization? Is there any reason that initialization couldn't happen twice for the same `System` object?

Thank you :-)

> Is there any reason that initialization couldn't happen twice for the same System object?

Conceptually, IMO because it doesn't make sense at the MAVSDK level. In terms of implementation, MAVSDK does some stuff for you in the background, so if you split the same connection between two systems, then all of that will be doubled, and will most likely conflict (`systemA` sends a command, `systemB` receives the ACK that looks like it was for itself, but is confused because it never sent a command in the first place, ...).

> unfortunately that's as much detail as I can give right now :(

Pretty hard to help then :laughing:. If I was to do multihoming, I would do it "in front" of MAVSDK, as a different component. MAVSDK would never know about it, it would just happen.
